correctness.rationale: Direct reconstruction of the one-indexed folding recursion f_b(2a)=f_{Tb}(a), f_b(2a+1)=(-1)^a b_0 shows S_b(i,2^k)=S_{T^(k-1)b}(ceil(i/2^(k-1)),2). Under displacement 2^k, reduced starts shift by exactly 2. All nonzero length-two sums reverse sign under this shift, hence equal consecutive block sums must be zero. Boolean E(a)=1_{f_{T^2c}(a)=-(-1)^a c_0} has alternating entries on odd a, proving no four consecutive zeros or ones. Natural parity-conditional sign and adjacent equal-pair densities follow by partitioning integer indices by exact two-adic valuation, controlling the tail <=2^-H; two- and three-run calculations give the asserted 1/4 and 1/16, with independent L=1 boundary. This proves every instruction sequence, rather than relying on finite prefixes. An independent bounded direct-bit check tested 16 periodic instructions, dyadic L<=32, 8192 starting positions, no fourth powers and proportions close to the asserted limits (not exact finite counts).
residual_risks: No independent formal proof certificate; natural density is not a per-prefix exact equality.

value.rationale: The restriction to powers of two has a structural dyadic-renormalization reason: every generalized paperfolding word has Abelian powers of arbitrarily high exponent at unrestricted periods, yet all dyadic fourth powers are impossible. Exact natural square/cube densities for an entire uncountable family of instruction sequences are useful finer local invariants, not merely abelian complexity or an arbitrary slice.
residual_risks: No statement about non-dyadic root lengths or exact finite-prefix occurrence counts is supported.

final_claim: For every instruction sequence b and each dyadic period L=2^k with k>=1, paperfolding block sums have values -2,0,2 with respective natural densities 1/4,1/2,1/4; Abelian-square/cube starts have densities 1/4 and 1/16, and Abelian fourth or higher powers cannot occur at any dyadic period. At L=1 the square/cube densities are 1/2 and 1/8, and fourth powers are still absent.
limitations: Dyadic root lengths only; arbitrary instructions included; finite prefix checks are diagnostic, not all-infinite proof; best-of-knowledge originality qualified.
